requirement:
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. If the required base directory cannot be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic.

The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
rationale:
The implementation in `src/config.rs` satisfies `user_location`, and the test covers the main cases. Two small gaps remain, listed at the end.

**Implementation**
- `user_config_path_from` (lines 566–579) handles Unix and Windows as the requirement specifies.
  - On Unix it uses `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when `absolute_directory` accepts it. That helper rejects an unset, empty or relative value, because `PathBuf::from("")` is not absolute.
  - Otherwise it uses `$HOME/.config`.
  - On Windows it uses `%APPDATA%`.
  - Every case appends `habeas/config.toml`.
- If the base directory can't be determined, `required_directory` returns an `io::Error` of kind `NotFound`. Its message says `cannot determine Habeas directory: {name} must be an absolute, nonempty path`, which is explanatory.
- `resolve_authoring` calls `user_config_path()?`, so an operation that needs user configuration fails with that diagnostic.
- `user_config_path()` takes no project or workspace argument and reads only environment variables via `ConfigPlatform::current()`. The location is therefore independent of the current project and can't be changed by project settings. The same file is used across projects.
- Workspace settings are handled separately by `load_workspace_config`, which the requirement cites as `workspace_location`.
- All the code that implements the requirement carries `{impl}` markers: `ConfigPlatform::current`, `user_config_path`, `user_config_path_from`, `absolute_directory` and `required_directory`.

**Tests**
`locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks` in `tests/configuration.rs` (lines 12–66) covers:
- an absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`;
- an empty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falling back to `$HOME/.config`;
- a relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falling back to `$HOME/.config`;
- the Windows `APPDATA` path;
- an error when no environment variables are set on Unix.

**Gaps**
- The tests only assert `is_err()`, not the diagnostic text.
- Requiring `APPDATA` and `HOME` to be absolute goes slightly beyond the literal wording. It is a reasonable reading of "cannot be determined", and it is shared with the state-location code.

text: :::{req} user_location
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. If the required base directory cannot be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
